To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the complete genome sequence of V. angullarum strain V.15 revealed the presence of two putative type IV pilus systems, 2) a mutant lacking the PilA pilin, the major pilin of one of these type IV pilus operons, did not affect the pathogenicity towards sea bass larvae, and 3) this indicates that type IV pili may have an additional role in V. angullarium pathogenesis, e.g. infection

(1) a V. angu illarum VIB 15 pilA mutant is avirulent towards sea bass larvae, (2) the pilA gene is located on a 1, 6 kb genomic fragment and (3) a second type IV pilus locus is present on the V. anguil l arum VIB15 chromosome.

(i) V. anguilla rum VIB15 is highly virulent towards D. labrax larvae, (ii) a V. angu- illarum VIB 15 pilA mutant, lacking the type IV pilin PilA, is not significantly less virulent towards D. labrax larvae compared to the wild type strain VIB15.

virulence factors of a bacterial pathogen, V. anguilla- rum, which causes vibriosis in marine fish.

the V. cholerae-like type IV pilus is not essential for virulence towards fish larvae, whereas the role of the PilA pilin in virulence remains unclear.
